enrichment.short_title: EIC bonus share issue void for common mistake
key_facts: EIC Services made a December 1999 bonus issue capitalising share premium to allot 99 bonus shares per ordinary share.
Neuberger J held many November 1999 shares were unpaid and shareholder approval was missing, but that s 35A could validate the issue.
Shareholder Jeremy Lee Barber appealed, arguing the bonus issue was void for common mistake and that s 35A did not apply.
The bonus resolution assumed all 137,555 shares were equally entitled and fully paid; in fact most November shares were nil paid.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Court of Appeal appeal with permission from Neuberger J on preliminary issues as to validity of a bonus share issue.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; the 15 December 1999 bonus issue was declared void because the interlinked defects made the assumed subject matter radically different, and s 35A did not apply as shareholders receiving bonus shares were not persons dealing with the company.
enrichment.ratio: Where a bonus issue proceeds on the mistaken footing that all shares are paid up and equally entitled, the cumulative defects can render the entire issue void for common mistake by analogy with contract law; a member receiving an internal bonus issue is not a person dealing with the company for s 35A purposes.

enrichment.short_title: Landfill tax: re-contouring below cap is not site restoration

enrichment.short_title: Illegal worker barred from race discrimination claim
key_facts: Mr V, a Croatian asylum seeker, falsely claimed he needed no work permit and worked as a trainee teacher while receiving benefits.

enrichment.short_title: English court jurisdiction to vary Jersey Hickory Trust
key_facts: During divorce and bankruptcy proceedings the wife sought to vary the Jersey Hickory Trust as a post-nuptial settlement under Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 s 24.
The trust deed chose Jersey law and exclusive Jersey jurisdiction; the husband and wife were removed as beneficiaries in January 2001.
Wilson J held the English court had jurisdiction; the husband appealed on Hague Convention and nuptial-settlement grounds.
Substantial disputed assets included proceeds from sale of an estate agency targeted by the wife's s 24 application.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Court of Appeal permission-to-appeal hearing on jurisdiction to vary a Jersey discretionary trust in ancillary relief proceedings.
enrichment.outcome: Permission granted but appeal dismissed; the English divorce court could apply s 24 despite Jersey proper-law and forum clauses, and removing the spouses as beneficiaries did not erase the settlement's post-nuptial character.
enrichment.ratio: Article 15 of the Hague Trusts Convention preserves mandatory forum conflict rules on the personal and proprietary effects of marriage, so s 24 variation powers are not ousted by trust exclusive-jurisdiction clauses; a settlement can remain post-nuptial where spouses retain protector powers and children remain beneficiaries.

enrichment.short_title: Mortgage shortfall claim time-barred after instalment default
key_facts: The Wilkinsons defaulted on monthly repayments under a 1988 legal charge; last payment was 31 July 1989.
West Bromwich sold the charged house in November 1990 leaving a shortfall of about £23,922.
It did not sue personally for the deficit until November 2002, more than twelve years later.
The deed covenant to pay by instalments did not expressly accelerate on default, but implied remedies existed.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Second appeal to the Court of Appeal on whether a county court shortfall claim was statute-barred under the Limitation Act 1980.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed and cross-appeal dismissed; the personal shortfall claim was barred twelve years after the cause of action accrued on instalment default, not from the later sale date.
enrichment.ratio: A mortgage shortfall remains the same debt secured by covenant and mortgage; the right to receive the principal accrued when instalments were defaulted and enforcement remedies arose, so ss 8 and 20(1) bar recovery more than twelve years later even after the security was sold.

key_facts: Madeleine Taylor, a childless aunt, made several substantial land and cash gifts to her nephew Philip Randall while frail and reliant on him.

enrichment.short_title: Harmondsworth fast-track detention lawful for Togo asylum seeker
key_facts: Mr Kpandang, a Togolese national, claimed asylum in April 2004 after arrest as an illegal entrant in Liverpool where he had a partner and newborn child.
The Home Office allocated his claim to Harmondsworth fast-track processing for nationals of listed generally unfounded countries.

Bennett J had suspended the asylum process; McCombe J heard the lawfulness challenge after release.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of Harmondsworth fast-track allocation and lawfulness of immigration detention pending asylum determination.
enrichment.outcome: Claim dismissed; detention was within Schedule 2 powers and published fast-track policy, and short detention for speedy asylum processing was a proportionate Article 8 interference on the facts.
enrichment.ratio: Harmondsworth fast-track use of single-male accommodation does not exclude claimants with UK family ties as a matter of policy; where detention is for efficient examination rather than absconding risk, Saadi principles support proportionate short detention even if Article 8 separation from family occurs.
